key_facts: Council Bill 245 proposes a rezoning from Gmc's 32grx5 to General Urban Residential Mixed Use five story.
The property is located at 2423-2490 South University in southeast Denver, within Council District six.
The current site contains commercial business and retail uses 1 to 2 stories built between 1951 and 1972.
There was a petition of protest filed by the neighborhood, which constitutes a legal protest under the zoning code.
The rezoning requires an affirmative vote of ten out of twelve council members to pass.
The planning board voted 9 to 0 to recommend support of this application.
The proposed rezoning is consistent with the University Park Neighborhood Plan and Blueprint Denver.
University Boulevard is identified as an enhanced transit corridor in Blueprint Denver.
The rezoning would allow for up to 70 feet in height, compared to the current allowance of 45 feet in the three storey district.
Staff concludes the proposed amendment will support uniform application of the district regulations and maintain public health, safety, and welfare.
The rezoning is justified due to changed conditions and the need for redevelopment.
The neighborhood context includes single family residential areas to the east and commercial areas to the west.
The proposed development includes 236 units, 25,000 square feet of retail, and parking below grade.
A traffic study was conducted by the developer and shared with the neighborhood, indicating that traffic volumes on University Boulevard would not be significantly impacted.
The project has generated significant public discussion and debate with both supporters and opponents expressing concerns about traffic, safety, and neighborhood character.
The University Park Community Council opposed the rezoning, stating that it does not align with the neighborhood plan and character.
The rezoning was initially considered in 2010 but was not approved due to the property being split among multiple owners.
The applicant, no doubt Colorado, recently acquired the majority of the block outside of a 7-Eleven.
The rezoning is part of a broader effort to encourage infill development and mixed-use projects along University Boulevard.
The rezoning proposal was supported by the City Planning Department and the developer's team.
The final vote on the rezoning passed with 13 affirmative votes.
